qa.question: Should GT1 to GT3 be 119 MW each instead of 149 MW?
qa.finding: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx) gives 119.0 MW for GT1 to GT3 and 87.6 MW for GT4 and GT5, where GEM has 149 MW and 108 MW. The Title V air permit (https://dep.gateway.ky.gov/eSearch.WebApi/api/documentGenerate/getDocument/10125517) rates each ABB GT 11N2 turbine at 115 MW at ISO conditions, which is a different measure and not EKPC's nameplate. I found no EKPC nameplate document.
qa.recommendation: Change GT1 to GT3 to 119.0 MW and GT4 and GT5 to 87.6 MW on the strength of the EIA table, unless a person can get EKPC's nameplate sheet. Ask the project manager whether EIA is acceptable here.
qa.note: I looked in the harvested permit index, the Title V permit and the EKPC 2025 integrated resource plan docket summary at https://psc.ky.gov/Case/ViewCaseFilings/2025-00087. The existing resources table of the plan itself was not opened because it was not in the harvested files. EIA also gives GT6 and GT7 as 94.9 MW and GT9 and GT10 as 108.2 MW, where GEM has 98 MW for each. Those values are reported as capacity findings on those units. The EKPC 2025 plan itself was searched through the commission case page and its existing resources table could not be matched to unit names. The permit lists GT-ratings under different unit numbers, so it cannot confirm nameplates. The Kentucky Division for Air Quality Title V permit text and the commission order were read in the first pass.
